transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

It is not normally a sign that the battery is flat, even if it shows full. 1. Switch it off; remove the battery if it is cordless (or unplug it). Empty the bin and check the bin inlet, wand and floorhead for trapped fluff, paper or a small object. A clear airway should let something small pass straight through. 2. Check the filter. If it looks dusty, wash it only in cold water, without detergent, then leave it to dry naturally for at least 24 hours before refitting. Even slightly damp filters can cause pulsing. 3. Turn the floorhead over and remove hair/thread from the brush bar. Make sure the roller turns freely by hand. A jammed roller can also make it cut in and out. If it runs steadily once those are clear and the filter is fully dry, that was the cause. If it still pulses with clear airways, a dry clean filter and no brush-bar jam, the next possibilities are battery protection or an internal motor/electronics fault; that is when repair assessment is sensible.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
its a v8 animal. no burning smell or heat or swelling tho. ill try the bin n filter first, its been a few days of this after i hoovered loads of dog hair n cat litter

The dog hair and cat litter timing makes an airflow restriction the front-runner. On a V8, pulsing is usually the protection system responding to a blocked airway or a clogged filter, rather than a failed battery. When you check it, pay particular attention to the narrow bin inlet/cyclone opening and the bend where the wand meets the floorhead; litter and compacted hair often lodge there. Also clear hair from the brush bar, but do this with the battery removed. If the filter needs washing, use cold water only and leave it somewhere warm and airy for a full 24 hours before trying it again. Do not refit it damp, as that alone can keep it pulsing. If it still pulses after the airway is clear and the filter is completely dry, the next useful divider is to run it briefly with the wand and floorhead removed. If it then runs steadily, the blockage is in the wand or cleaner head; if it still pulses with just the main body and bin fitted, battery protection or an internal motor/electronics issue becomes more likely and a repair assessment is sensible.
ok did the bin n filter. emptied it, was full of dog hair, still pulsin. filter was never washed lol, water came out black. left it overnight on the radiator, pulses way less but still a bit

The much reduced pulsing after washing the filter is strong evidence that restricted airflow is the cause, not the battery. Overnight may not be enough: the filter needs a full 24 hours from washing and must be completely dry before use; a damp filter can still make it pulse. Once it is fully dry, try it briefly with only the main body and bin fitted — no wand or cleaner head. - Runs steadily: there is still a blockage or brush-bar restriction in the wand or cleaner head.
• Still pulses: check the bin inlet/cyclone openings again for compacted hair or litter. If those are clear, an internal motor/electronics issue becomes the more likely cause and it would need a repair assessment. Do not keep running it with a damp filter fitted.
ok tried it with just the handheld body, still does it but a bit less. what next?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Next, treat the filter as not yet proved dry. The big improvement after washing it points strongly to airflow restriction, and an overnight dry on a radiator can still leave moisture deep in it. 1. Remove the filter again and leave it to air-dry for a full 24 hours from washing; it must feel completely dry throughout before it goes back in. Do not run the vacuum without the filter.
2. With the battery removed, inspect the bin inlet and the small cyclone/shroud openings above the bin. Remove any packed hair or litter gently with a dry soft brush or wooden/plastic tool — no water into the main body.
3. Refit the completely dry filter and test it again with just the main body and bin fitted. If it then runs steadily, the cause was the wet/clogged filter or debris in the cyclone. If it still pulses in that bare-body test with a genuinely clean, fully dry filter and clear inlet, an internal motor/electronics fault becomes more likely than the battery; that needs a Dyson repair assessment rather than more cleaning.
checked the bin inlet n cyclone bit, only a bit dusty so i wiped it. filter is the same as before, pulses way less but still a bit. what else can i try?

Yes — the next sensible thing to try is the battery connection, as the obvious inlet/cyclone area has now been checked and it still pulses with the handheld body alone. 1. Remove the battery with the vacuum switched off. Wipe the metal contacts on the battery and main body with a clean, dry cloth. Check for dirt, bent contacts or green/white corrosion; do not use water or spray cleaner.
2. Refit the battery firmly, charge it normally, then test again briefly. If it is genuinely completely dry and it still pulses with only the body and bin fitted, the likely fault moves to the battery protection system or the main motor/electronics. Those are internal repair items rather than something to dismantle at home.
ok wiped the contacts n tried again, not sure what that changes tbh. did u want me to look down the wand too? its still pulsin a bit
AI service unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
hello? got an error. shall i look down the wand too?

Yes — look down the wand too. It is worth clearing because dog hair and cat litter commonly form a plug in the wand, floorhead neck or around the brush bar. 1. Remove the battery first. Take off the wand and floorhead, then look through the wand from both ends. A coin should pass straight through; if it does not, there is a blockage.
2. Check the narrow inlet/neck on the floorhead and remove any packed hair or litter. Turn the brush bar by hand and clear wrapped hair or thread if it is stiff. A blockage there would explain pulsing when using the full vacuum, but it does not fully explain it pulsing with the body alone. The strong improvement after washing the filter still makes a filter that is damp or not fully clean the leading cause. If the wand and head are clear, leave the filter air-drying until it has had a full 24 hours and feels dry all the way through, then retry it. If it still pulses with only the body and bin fitted after that, the remaining likely fault is the internal motor/protection electronics or battery protection; that is a Dyson repair-job rather than more home dismantling.
ok looked down the wand, big clump of hair and cat litter stuck at the bottom where the head goes on, pulled it out. its fine now, proper suction, no pulsin

That was the cause — the hair and cat-litter plug at the bottom of the wand was restricting airflow, so the vacuum was pulsing to protect itself. Proper suction and no pulsing suggests it. For prevention, empty the bin before it gets packed and occasionally check both ends of the wand and the floorhead neck, especially after pet hair or litter. Let the washed filter finish air-drying fully before regular use as well. Anything else you need help with?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

candidates: Restricted airflow from a blockage or dirty/damp filter (high)
Jam in the motorised floorhead brush bar (medium)
Battery protection or a failing battery (low)
